```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(easyNIS)
```

## Flag diagnoses and procedures

The analyst supplies literal code prefixes. Each slot is tested separately;
punctuation, spaces, and case in the supplied prefixes are normalized.

```{r flags}
nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50") |>
  nis_flag_dx(principal_hf = "I50", position = "principal") |>
  nis_flag_pr(ablation = "02L")
nis |> dplyr::count(heart_failure, principal_hf, ablation) |> dplyr::collect()
```

The table shows synthetic discharge counts for each flag combination. To make
a principal-only diagnosis flag, call `nis_flag_dx()` with
`position = "principal"`; use `"secondary"` for slots after the principal one.
`nis_flag_pr()` supports `"any"` and `"principal"`.

## Classify diagnoses and procedures with CCSR

`nis_add_ccsr()` matches complete ICD-10 codes to the bundled AHRQ mappings
in DuckDB. An any-slot search returns a list of distinct categories for
each discharge. Supply `categories` to keep only the categories relevant to
the study. For a mutually exclusive grouping by principal diagnosis, use
`position = "default"` to return the inpatient default category.

```{r ccsr}
nis |>
  nis_add_ccsr(categories = "CIR019", name = "hf_categories") |>
  nis_add_ccsr(position = "default", name = "principal_ccsr") |>
  dplyr::filter(length(hf_categories) > 0L) |>
  dplyr::count(principal_ccsr) |>
  dplyr::collect()
```

Use `type = "pr"` for procedures. The default release selection covers Q4
2015 and calendar years 2016–2024 with the bundled v2025.1. ICD-9 and years
outside the bundled coverage yield missing results. Pin `version = "2025.1"`
to use the same definitions across years and to include Q1–Q3 2025 if `DQTR`
is present. Report the CCSR version in the study methods. [Agency for
Healthcare Research and Quality, Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project.
Clinical Classifications Software Refined (CCSR), v2025.1, November
2024.](https://hcup-us.ahrq.gov/toolssoftware/ccsr/ccsr_archive.jsp)

## Add procedure timing

Procedure timing compares matching procedure slots with the corresponding
`PRDAY` fields. This small invented data frame makes the slot relationship
visible.

```{r timing}
toy <- data.frame(
  I10_PR1 = c("02UG0JZ", "02UG0JZ", "02UG0JZ"),
  I10_PR2 = c("0JH604Z", "0JH604Z", "0JH604Z"),
  PRDAY1 = c(0L, 2L, 0L), PRDAY2 = c(1L, 1L, NA_integer_)
)
nis_flag_pr_timing(toy, "02UG0", "0JH60", relation = "after")
```

The flag is true when an outcome procedure is documented after the earliest
index procedure. Missing or sentinel days need an explicit `missing_day`
policy. `nis_audit_prday()` summarizes how often matching slots have a
known day.

## Count cohort steps

Define the eligibility rules once in `nis_attrition()`. With `.design = TRUE`,
the baseline includes discharges with valid survey design fields. Missing
criterion values exclude discharges at that step. Inject the combined rule
with `!!nis_attrition_cohort(flow)` to use the same eligibility criteria in
`nis_design()`.

```{r attrition}
nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50")
flow <- nis_attrition(
  nis, adults = AGE >= 18, heart_failure = heart_failure, .design = TRUE
)
flow

design <- nis_design(nis, cohort = !!nis_attrition_cohort(flow), keep = LOS)
dplyr::summarise(design, discharges = srvyr::unweighted(dplyr::n()))
```

Pass the same input to both calls so the last unweighted attrition count is
the survey domain denominator. The design retains the sampling structure of
hospital-years with zero eligible discharges. Leave `.design` at its default
when the attrition table should start with every discharge in the input.
For alternate diagnosis positions and changes over time, see [Code transitions
and sensitivity](code-transitions.html).

## Record eligibility across the 2015 transition

Supply named code criteria in `.codes` to use the same definitions for
eligibility and the transition audit. The code criteria run in list order
after the logical criteria in `...`. Here the first code step finds a match
in any diagnosis slot and the second requires a principal match. These
definitions illustrate the workflow on invented data.

```{r era-eligibility}
nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2015))
prefixes <- list(icd9 = c("123", "12345", "V0001"), icd10 = c("I50", "Z515"))
flow <- nis_attrition(
  nis,
  adults = AGE >= 18,
  .codes = list(
    matching_dx = list(type = "dx", system = "both", position = "any", codes = prefixes),
    principal_dx = list(type = "dx", system = "both", position = "principal", codes = prefixes)
  ),
  .design = TRUE
)
flow
attr(flow, "nis_criteria")

design <- nis_design(nis, cohort = !!nis_attrition_cohort(flow), keep = c(AGE, LOS))
fit <- survey::svyglm(LOS ~ AGE, design = design)
stats::nobs(fit)
```

The criteria table records the system and slot rule for Methods. Here the
last attrition count equals the number of observations in the model because
`AGE` and `LOS` are complete among eligible discharges. See the
[quarterly audit of these criteria](code-transitions.html#reuse-cohort-criteria).

## Save a cohort for another session

Pass the full lazy sample and the eligibility rule to `nis_write_cohort()`.
Keep the columns you expect to use in later analyses. The writer creates a
new directory with yearly Parquet parts and saves the eligibility expression,
source years, and easyNIS version in each part's metadata.

```{r save-cohort}
nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50")
path <- nis_write_cohort(nis, heart_failure & AGE >= 50, tempfile(),
                         keep = c(AGE, LOS))

# In a later session
design <- nis_design(nis_open(path), keep = c(AGE, LOS), annualize = TRUE)
design |>
  dplyr::filter(AGE >= 65) |>
  dplyr::summarise(discharges = srvyr::survey_total())
```

The saved cohort carries one placeholder per sampled hospital-year with no
eligible discharge. This preserves the survey variance structure, including
whole strata and years where the cohort is empty. Annualization still uses
all years with valid design records. Keep the original design run if you need
its invalid-design exclusion counts or full-sample quarter coverage.

Apply additional patient filters to the survey design after reopening.
When inspecting raw Parquet rows, use `dplyr::filter(.in_cohort)` before
counting discharges. To re-save a cohort with fewer columns, pass its reopened
query to `nis_write_cohort()` and omit `cohort`. To change the eligibility rule,
return to the source sample.

## Common pitfalls

> **Common pitfalls**
>
> - A prefix is not a validated clinical code set. Define, document, and
>   review it for the study question.
> - A cross-year definition may span different code systems. Do not assume
>   code counts are comparable across the 2015 transition.
> - Unknown procedure days are not equivalent to day zero; choose and report a
>   missing-day policy.
